skill.name: update-docs
skill.description: Updates project documentation such as feature specs, database design notes, error code lists, and README files.
skill.summary: Guides structured updates to project documentation while preserving existing Markdown organization.
skill.author: Crearize

security_audit.summary: All eight static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced examples, and Japanese prose. The skill describes a documentation update workflow and shows no prompt injection, data exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: - 対象: `README.md` または各ディレクトリのREADME.md

static_findings.pattern: [HEURISTIC] High file entropy (6.19 bits) - possible binary/encrypted content

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 17 is inline Markdown showing a target documentation path. It is not Ruby backtick execution and contains no shell command or interpolation.
Line 21 is inline Markdown showing the database design document path. It is documentation text, not command execution.
Line 25 is inline Markdown showing the error code document path. No executable command, shell substitution, or Ruby backtick use appears there.
Line 29 is inline Markdown naming README targets. It contains file paths only and does not invoke a shell.
Lines 33-36 contain a fenced bash example with a read-only cat command. This is not Ruby backtick execution and includes no destructive or network action.
The finding spans Markdown prose after a code fence, not an executable backtick expression. The text describes preserving structure and checking Markdown syntax.
Lines 48-60 are a fenced Markdown completion report template. The placeholders describe report fields and do not execute commands.
SKILL.md is readable UTF-8 Markdown with Japanese prose and short fenced examples. No binary, encrypted payload, encoded blob, or obfuscated content was found.

content.value_statement: Project documentation often falls behind implementation changes. This skill guides focused updates to specs, database notes, error lists, and README files.
actual_capabilities: Identifies supported document types for feature, database, error, and README updates.
Maps each document type to the expected project file path.
Reads the existing document before applying requested updates.
Preserves existing document structure and Markdown formatting.
Provides a completion report with document type, path, and update summary.
limitations: It only defines workflows for documentation files listed in the skill.
It does not create tests, application code, or database migrations.
It does not validate links, diagrams, or Markdown rendering with external tools.
It requires the user to provide update content and a document type.

use_cases.title: Refresh Feature Specifications
use_cases.description: Update a feature specification after behavior, requirements, or acceptance criteria change.

use_cases.title: Maintain Database Design Notes
use_cases.description: Keep database design documentation aligned with schema changes and new data relationships.

use_cases.title: Revise README and Error Guides
use_cases.description: Document new setup steps, usage notes, or error codes after a release.

prompt_templates.title: Update a README
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the README documentation with these setup changes: [describe changes]. Keep the current structure and Markdown style.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single README update.

prompt_templates.title: Revise a Feature Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the feature specification for [feature name]. Add these behavior changes and acceptance criteria: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Synchronize Database Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the database design document with these schema changes: [tables, fields, relationships]. Preserve existing section order.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after schema design work.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the relevant docs after this release: [release notes]. Cover feature specs, README changes, and error code updates as needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request spanning multiple documentation areas.

output_examples.input: Update the README with new installation steps and environment setup notes.
output: README selected as the target document.
Installation and environment sections updated while preserving the existing layout.
Completion report lists the updated path and summary of changes.

output_examples.input: Update the database design document with a new audit log table.
output: Database design document selected as the target.
Audit log details added in the existing database documentation structure.
Completion report identifies the document path and the applied update.

output_examples.input: Add a new validation error code to the error documentation.
output: Error code list selected as the target document.
New error information inserted with matching Markdown formatting.
Completion report summarizes the added error code entry.

best_practices: Provide the document type and the exact update scope.
Include source decisions, requirements, or release notes with the request.
Review the final Markdown diff before committing the change.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to update unrelated application code.
Do not provide vague update text without a target document.
Do not use it to read arbitrary files outside documented project paths.

faq.question: Which documents can this skill update?
faq.answer: It supports feature specifications, database design notes, error code lists, and README files.

faq.question: Does it preserve existing Markdown structure?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow asks the agent to keep the existing structure and Markdown format.

faq.question: Can it create application code?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on documentation updates, not code implementation.

faq.question: Does it validate Markdown rendering?
faq.answer: No. It asks for syntax review, but it does not define an external renderer or validator.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should I include in a request?
faq.answer: Include the document type, target feature or area, and the exact content changes.
